conclusion: Addressed. Finite Tailwind3/Uno plans skip the main-process Tailwind resolve/require; the existing finite path loads those toolchains only in its bounded confined worker. No new plausible vulnerability identified in this focused change.

evidence.detail: compile is a type-only optional declaration; typeof import does not load a module at runtime.
The !runtime.cssPlan guard now encloses both the Tailwind entry resolve/realpath check (line65) and require (line66). A finite plan cannot execute either host operation.
A finite plan obtains cssCompiler, which always returns a compiler closure or rejects. Failure propagates; it does not fall back to the host compiler.
Virtual Uno entry still calls the finite compiler directly.
Stylesheets use finiteCss first; the else branch for the legacy compiler is reached only when finiteCss is absent.
Legacy compile call is unchanged apart from TypeScript non-null assertion. Its Tailwind4 load/check, fixed loadStylesheet adapter and source behavior remain unchanged when no CSS plan exists.
Unchanged since prior review: compiler closure routes to runCssWorker; line156 sets resource limits and line158 the deadline.
Unchanged since prior review: synchronous CJS/ESM realpath hooks are registered before trusted toolchain loads at lines12,15,18.
